name: zeroes to the end, in place
hook: Move every zero to the end of an array, in place, without shifting anything twice.
hook_slide: Move the zeroes to the end. *No second array.*
hook_sub: And without shifting the whole array on every zero.
caption: Move Zeroes: push every 0 to the end, keep the other numbers in order, use O(1) extra space.
The tempting way: find a zero, shift everything after it left, drop the zero at the end. Correct, and accidentally quadratic.
The insight: zeroes are all identical, so they don't need carrying. Compact the non-zeroes to the front with a write pointer, then fill the tail with zeroes.
On {n} numbers with every other one a zero, that's {ref_writes} writes against {shuffle_writes} for the shuffle: {ratio} times fewer.
There's a one-pass swap version too. Which would you write? 👇
cta: Then try the one-pass swap version and its three-region invariant.

p: O(1) auxiliary space: building a new array fails the requirement.
Find a zero, shift everything after it one step left, place the zero at the end.
Correct, and *accidentally quadratic*: every zero moves the rest of the array.
They are all identical, so they can be *reconstructed*.
Compact the non-zeroes to the front, in order. Then fill the tail with zeroes.
Everything before `w` is a non-zero, in order. Whatever is left past `w` gets overwritten with zeroes.

slides.h: {n} numbers, every other one a zero
p: One write per slot, however many zeroes there are.
